findings.title: Async legacy write inherits request context and will be cancelled
findings.body: In Create (line 51) and identically in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163), the background goroutine does context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context. When the API handler returns, that parent context is cancelled, which immediately cancels the child. So the intended asynchronous write to legacy will almost always be cancelled/timed out and never complete, silently diverging legacy and unified storage. The async work must be detached, e.g. with context.WithoutCancel or context.Background, before applying the 10s timeout.

findings.title: Create replicates stale input object to legacy instead of stored result
findings.body: Create writes to Storage and gets back `created`, but the async legacy write calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) with the original input `obj`. The storage result typically contains assigned UID, resourceVersion, creationTimestamp and defaults/mutations. Legacy will therefore receive a stale object missing those fields, permanently diverging the two stores. It should replicate `created` (ideally a deep copy, since it is shared with the returned response and the goroutine).

findings.title: Update reuses single-use UpdatedObjectInfo for two stores concurrently
findings.body: Update calls d.Storage.Update with `objInfo` synchronously and then reuses the same `objInfo` in an async goroutine for d.Legacy.Update. The previous implementation fetched the updated object once and wrapped it in an updateWrapper so both stores wrote the identical object. Re-invoking UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject a second time can compute a different object, fail on resourceVersion/concurrency checks, or race with request-scoped state. The storage result should be captured and replayed to legacy instead of re-executing objInfo.

findings.title: Storage errors recorded as legacy metrics (Create/Update)
findings.body: On synchronous storage failure, Create line 45 and Update line 129 call recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) with startStorage. The failure was in Storage, not legacy, and no legacy call was made. This misattributes latency/error metrics, hiding storage failures and inflating legacy error rates. They should call recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

findings.title: Delete storage metric uses object name as kind label
findings.body: Delete success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...) passing the object `name` where the `kind` label (options.Kind) is expected. Every deleted object name becomes a distinct metric label value, causing high cardinality and making kind-based dashboards/alerts useless. It should pass options.Kind like the error path and other methods do.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage metric
findings.body: Inside the async legacy goroutine for DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will therefore be attributed to unified storage, corrupting both sets of metrics. It should call recordLegacyDuration like Create/Delete/Update do.

findings.title: Delete discards enriched logger when building context
findings.body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method)` but then does klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), discarding those values. All downstream storage/legacy logs and context-derived logging lose name/kind/method correlation, unlike Create/Get/Update/DeleteCollection which propagate `log`. It should pass `log`.

findings.title: Mode3 tests never verify async legacy writes
findings.body: Mode3 writes are now asynchronous via `go func()`, but TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection only assert the synchronous storage return value and return immediately. They never wait for or assert the legacy mock was called, and several cases don't even set up a legacy expectation. A broken or missing legacy replication (wrong object, cancelled context, wrong metrics) would still pass. Tests need synchronization/assertion of the background legacy call.
